'''Oh Se-jung''' ({{Korean|hangul=오세정}}; born February 17, 1954) is a South Korean politician and physicist. He has served as the director of the Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies, the first president of the [[Institute for Basic Science]], and the 27th president of [[Seoul National University]].

==Education==
Oh entered [[Kyunggi High School]] of [[Gangnam District]] in 1968 and graduated in 1971. He next graduated from [[Seoul National University]] in 1975 with a Bachelor of Physics. Moving to the U.S., he did a combined M.S. and Ph.D. in physics at [[Stanford University]] graduating in 1981.

==Career==
Staying in California, Oh worked as a researcher at the Palo Alto Institute of [[Xerox]] until 1984, in which he returned to Korea to work as a professor at the Department of Physics and Astronomy in Seoul National University (SNU). He then worked as a research at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] from 1987. During this time, he was a visiting researcher and professor at the [[University of Michigan]] and [[University of Tokyo]], respectively. Returning to SNU, he was the head of the Planning Lab under the College of National Sciences. He later served as the director of the Multi-Systems Research Center for Excellence of the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (South Korea)|Ministry of Science and Technology]] with the last several years overlapping as the director and later vice chairman of the Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies. His next position was as the founding president of the [[Institute for Basic Science]]. He left to pursue the president's office at SNU, where he scored highly in the policy evaluation<ref>{{cite web |url= https://news.joins.com/article/14548105 |script-title=ko:서울대 총장 후보 정책평가 … 오세정 교수 1위 |last= 이 |first= 상화 |date= 28 April 2014 |website=[[JoongAng Ilbo]] |publisher= |access-date= 17 January 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://en.snu.ac.kr/media-coverage?bm=v&bbsidx=120323 |title= Professor OH Se Jung Ranked Highest in SNU Presidential Candidates' Policy Evaluation |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 28 April 2014 |website= [[Seoul National University]] |publisher= |access-date= 16 January 2020 |quote= }}</ref> before losing to Sung Nak-in, who became the 26th president of SNU. Oh worked in politics before again applying for and eventually getting the position at SNU as the 27th president<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.useoul.edu/president/message |title= Message from the President |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= February 2019 |website= [[Seoul National University]] |publisher= |access-date= 7 January 2020 |quote= |language= }}</ref> He was inaugurated on February 8, 2019,<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.useoul.edu/president/speeches?bm=v&bbsidx=125921 |title= Inaugural Address of President Oh Se-Jung |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 11 February 2019 |website= [[Seoul National University]] |publisher= |access-date= 7 January 2020 |quote=}}</ref> while also becoming the 10th chairman of the ({{ill|Seoul National University Foundation|ko|서울대학교발전재단}}).
